problem: Find a vector that's tangent to the curve $r(t)=⟨t+\frac{1}{t},\,t-\frac{1}{t}⟩$ at the point where $t=1.$
worked_solution:
At the point where $t=1$,  the vector ${r}^{′}(1)$ is tangent to the curve.

Let's calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t-\frac{1}{t})⟩ \\  & =⟨1-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,1+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(1) & =⟨1-\frac{1}{{1}^{2}},\,1+\frac{1}{{1}^{2}}⟩ \\  & =⟨1-1,\,1+1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a tangent vector to the given curve at the point where $t=1$  is  $⟨0,\,2⟩.$
